dissections.verse: For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.

breakdown.meaning: The Creator, the Trinity - Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The one true God who is love itself.
Loved to such an immense degree. This is agape love - unconditional, sacrificial, eternal love.
All of humanity, every person ever created. Not just believers, but everyone - showing God's universal love.
God took action. Love is shown through sacrifice and giving, not just words.
Jesus Christ, the second persons of the Trinity. God's most precious gift - His own Son.
An open invitation to all. Faith (belief) is the key - trusting in Christ's sacrifice.
Will be saved from spiritual death and eternal separation from God.
Forever with God in heaven. Not just living forever, but living in relationship with God eternally.

dissections.context: Jesus speaking to Nicodemus, a Pharisee who came to Him at night seeking truth.

dissections.verse: The Lord is my shepherd, I lack nothing.

breakdown.meaning: Yahweh, the covenant name of God. The personal, faithful God of Israel.
A shepherd guides, protects, provides for, and cares for sheep. This is personal - 'my' shepherd, not distant.
Complete contentment and provision. When God is our shepherd, He supplies all our true needs.

dissections.context: David, who was a shepherd himself, wrote this psalm reflecting on God's care for him.

dissections.verse: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.

breakdown.meaning: Personal capability - but not in our own strength. The emphasis is on what follows.
Everything God calls us to do. Not necessarily everything we want, but everything in God's will for us.
The source of our strength. Not by our power, but by being united with Jesus.
Christ actively empowers us. Present tense - He is strengthening us right now, continually.

dissections.context: Paul wrote this from prison, having learned contentment in all circumstances - plenty or need.

dissections.verse: And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose.

breakdown.meaning: This is certain truth, not wishful thinking. Believers can be confident in this promise.
Every circumstance - good and bad, joyful and painful. Nothing is outside God's sovereign plan.
God is actively involved. He doesn't just allow things, He orchestrates them for purpose.
Ultimate good - our spiritual maturity and God's glory. Not always what feels good, but what is truly good.
Believers who have a relationship with God. Those who are in covenant with Him.
Chosen by God for His plans. Our lives fit into God's greater redemptive purpose.

dissections.context: Paul reassuring believers that nothing can separate them from God's love, even suffering.

dissections.verse: Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.

breakdown.meaning: A personal invitation from Jesus. Not to a religion or rules, but to a person - Him.
Exhausted, tired from life's struggles. Jesus welcomes those who are spiritually and physically drained.
Carrying heavy loads - sin, guilt, anxiety, legalism, life's troubles.
Jesus promises relief. Not just physical rest, but peace for the soul. This is His gift, not earned.

dissections.context: Jesus contrasting His gentle way with the heavy burdens the Pharisees placed on people.
